title: Recommendations for determining the validity of consumer wearable heart rate devices: expert statement and checklist of the INTERLIVE Network
authors: Mühlen JM, Stang J, Lykke Skovgaard E, Judice PB, Molina-Garcia P, Johnston W, Sardinha LB, Ortega FB, Caulfield B, Bloch W, Cheng S, Ekelund U, Brønd JC, Grøntved A, Schumann M
population: Expert statement built on a PRISMA-based systematic review (44 eligible articles), a wider literature review and expert opinion, on PPG-based consumer HR wearables
findings: Methodological differences and shortcomings in the validation process hamper comparability of the validity of consumer PPG heart-rate wearables.

A PRISMA-based systematic review found 44 eligible articles; together with a wider literature review and expert opinion it produced a validation framework with six domains: target population, criterion measure, index measure, testing conditions, data processing and statistical analysis.
Checklists are provided to guide validation protocol development and reporting.
limitations: Methodological guidance, not a device ranking; the abstract gives no accuracy figures; recommendations rest partly on expert opinion.
implications: Judge any wearable-validity evidence the engine relies on against this framework (criterion measure, testing conditions, statistics) before turning it into a rule.
No numeric parameter is justified by this statement.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, BJSM, published online 4 Jan 2021 (print Jul 2021), first author Muhlen, 15 authors. Abstract read in Europe PMC. Rated A because it includes a PRISMA systematic review, but it is methodology guidance rather than accuracy evidence.
